beneficiaries: ship lessors, ship leasing managers, ship agents, ship managers, ship brokers, commodity traders

policydecision_details: The National Anti-Doping Organisation of Cabo Verde (ONAD-CV) has secured US$73,000 in funding from UNESCO’s Fund for the Elimination of Doping in Sport. This project, titled 'Strengthening Anti-Doping Capacity in West and Central Africa: A Strategic Initiative', was approved on 27 October in New Delhi. The initiative is designed to run for 12 months and aims to enhance the technical and institutional capacities of anti-doping organizations in Africa’s Zones II and III. Activities will include training, technical capacity-building in Praia, and the development of tailored improvement plans for participating countries.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative was developed by ONAD-CV to address the need for strengthened anti-doping frameworks across West and Central Africa, specifically targeting capacity building and the sharing of best practices among regional anti-doping organizations.
decision_making_institution: National Anti-Doping Organisation of Cabo Verde (ONAD-CV)
beneficiaries: Anti-doping organisations in Africa’s Zones II and III

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding on mango exports to China, with shipments beginning on the following year.

This Decree establishes the specific technical criteria used to classify the size of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Lao PDR. Its primary objective is to clarify these classifications to ensure that government promotion policies are targeted effectively and support the sustainable development of the MSME sector. The size of an enterprise is determined based on three main indicators across the sectors of production, commerce (trade), and services: Average number of employees per year; Total value of assets; Total annual business revenue. If a single enterprise meets criteria for multiple size categories, the total annual business revenue serves as the deciding factor.

This Decree establishes the regulations for the management, monitoring, and use of the MSME Promotion Fund in the Lao PDR. The fund is a non-profit state financial entity designed to provide financial and technical support to micro, small, and medium enterprises to enhance their competitiveness and contribution to the national economy. The fund is capitalized through state budget allocations, grants from domestic and international organizations, interest from loans, and other legal income sources. Financial assistance is provided through low-interest loans (via commercial banks or financial institutions), credit guarantees, and technical grants for capacity building and product development. To access the fund, enterprises must be officially registered MSMEs that comply with relevant laws and have viable business plans or technical projects.

This Decision establishes a regulatory framework for managing the movement of specific goods across Lao borders, covering temporary imports, temporary exports, re-exports, and transit activities. It aims to ensure that these activities comply with national laws, protect national security and social order, and prevent the illegal domestic sale of goods intended for export. Specifically, the Decision categorizes goods into three lists: those requiring prior authorization, prohibited goods, and reserved goods. The technical annexes detail regulated items such as timber, vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), rough diamonds, and hazardous chemicals.

This Act provides for prevention of certain harmful activities related to the production, storage, transfer, transportation, supply, distribution and marketing of foodstuff. The Act makes it an offence for a person to manufacture or market food by removing or altering any natural ingredient; mixing artificial ingredients harmful to human health; or carry on any business without license. The Act prohibits and penalises stocking of foodstuff in excess of prescribed quantities. Any person supplying foodstuff to government warehouse which is mixed with old or expired foodstuff, or illegally procured, or altered in quantity or quality, shall be punishable under the Act. The Act further prohibits publishing false information relating to foodstuff or distributing bags of foodstuff from government warehouse without the appropriate seal. The Food Inspector is given powers to enter and inspect any premises and on having reasonable grounds, seal any place and seize food items. The Act provides for establishment of Special Food Courts and allows certain offences committed under the Act to be tried by mobile courts.

This Regulation amends the Regulation no. 26 of 2021 concerning the organisation of the agricultural sector, in order to: improve the role of the agricultural sector in the national development; increase productivity of the sector and thus realise food and energy security; strengthen the role of the State-owned enterprises. Amendments of article 3 of the main Regulation concern the maximum area limitation for plantation of palm oil, coconut, rubber, cocoa, coffee, sugar cane and tobacco.

This Decision is developed in accordance with the Law on Processing Industry. It establishes the comprehensive regulations and technical standards for the establishment, operation, and management of processing factories in the Lao PDR. The Decision defines the requirements for site selection, construction standards, and the technical documentation needed to obtain a factory establishment license. It outlines the procedures for applying for and renewing factory operation licenses, including the mandatory safety and environmental certifications required before production can begin. It mandates strict adherence to industrial safety protocols, waste management systems (liquid and solid), and air quality standards to minimize the impact on surrounding communities and the environment. In addition, the Decision makes provisions on inspection, labor and hygiene , and the general welfare of factory staff.

This document, GB 31608—2023, sets national food safety standards for tea in China. It is a mandatory standard. It defines tea types, specifies quality requirements for raw materials, sensory attributes, and mandates compliance with pollutant and pesticide residue limits. No food additives are allowed in tea production.

These Rules are framed pursuant to the powers under section 20 of Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995. These Rules aim to ensure sustainable development and prevent environmental degradation in Bangladesh by regulating the activities that may have adverse impacts on the environment and human health. Rule 3 provides for application by any person who has suffered loss due to environmental pollution and the same shall be disposed of within 30 working days. Rule 4 provides for the format of Notice to an owner, occupier or agent for collection of samples of air, water, soil or other substances. Rule 5 requires industrial projects and units to be classified based on their activities, pollution, and potential harm to the environment and health into Green, Yellow, Orange and Red categories. The Rules further lay down the procedure to obtain environmental clearance and location clearance certificate and the validity thereof. The Rules lay down the criteria and guidelines for conducting EIA and preparing environmental management plan. It also contains provisions for appeals, the appointment of appellate authority and the procedure to be followed by such authority. Rules 31 and 32 provide environmental standards for water quality, liquid waste emission etc. Rule 33 pertains to construction, approval and operation of liquid/sewage waste treatment plants of industrial establishments and projects. The Rules also provide for fees in respect of the services provided and mode of payment for the same.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: This Regulation, in order to implement the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1), Article 37, Article 45, Article 46 paragraph (3), Article 47 paragraph (4), Article 51, Article 53 paragraph (5), Article 61, and Article 63 of the Government Regulation no. 66 of 2014 concerning Environmental Health, provides for detailing environmental health quality standards in air, water, food, soil and specifically: efforts to protect public health, technical requirements for waste management processes, control of diseases-carrying animals, procedures and efforts to reduce climate change’s threats, and to prevent natural disasters. The Regulation concerns: health requirements; drinking water; hygiene and sanitation procedures; recreational use of water; public bathing water; ambient and indoor air; soil quality; food and food additives; processed food ready to eat; diseases carrying animals; hazardous and toxic substances; waste management. Matters covered by the Regulation include: definition of environmental health quality standards for air, water, food, soil and disease-carrying animals; healthcare measures and sanitation procedures; risk assessment and analysis; waste management and public health protection; monitoring and supervision procedures; specific requirements for waste originating from health service facilities; wastewater pollution; storage and transportation of waste; biosecurity measures concerning disease-carrying animals; use of One Health approach in the implementation of environmental health standards.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: This Decision establishes the technical standards and procedural steps for developing and implementing forest management plans at the village level across the Lao PDR. It aims to empower local communities to manage forest resources sustainably, ensuring the protection of biodiversity and ecosystems while supporting rural livelihoods. The Decision provides a structured framework for identifying forest categories—such as protection, conservation, and utility forests—within village boundaries to prevent land-use conflicts and illegal logging. The Decision details the seven-step process for village forest planning, which includes data collection, boundary demarcation, and the drafting of local regulations. It mandates the active participation of village authorities and Front for National Development representatives in the consultation process to ensure social consensus. Furthermore, the Decision outlines the requirements for monitoring and evaluation, specifying that plans must be reviewed and approved by District Offices of Agriculture and Forestry to ensure they align with national forestry strategies and the 2019 Forestry Law.

This Presidential Regulation provides for strengthening the implementation of the agrarian reform, as a national strategic program to create justice in land ownership and management, to improve land distribution, and to resolve agrarian conflicts. According to the Regulation, the agrarian reform provides for achieving a fair and prosperous society, through the redistribution of land, the legalisation of assets, and the implementation of targeted strategies and programmes. The Regulation focuses on the following objects of the agrarian reform: the land controlled by the State, the land owned or utilised by the local communities, for redistribution or legalisation purposes. The Regulation covers the following matters: land rights, as the legal relationship between the right holder and the land, including the control to own, use and exploit the space above the land, and the space below the ground; forest area; State forests; production forest area. The Regulation describes: the procedures and requirements for redistributing land to the subjects of agrarian reform, including: identification, measurement, mapping, determination, and certification of land rights; the purpose and implementation of a joint survey, conducted by the Ministry of Forestry and Agrarian Affairs, in coordination with local authorities, in order to improve redistribution of land that originates from the release of forest areas, and to determine the pattern of conflict resolution and land redistribution, in forest and non-forest areas, non-forest areas, State-owned enterprises assets,. Further matters covered by this Regulation concern: criteria and conditions for various types of asset legalisation, including: land certification, land titling for transmigration areas, and land administration for customary and communal lands; the creation of a regional task force to facilitate the resolution of land conflicts, the integration of assets and the implementation of the reform; monitoring, controlling, and reporting of the agrarian reform; funding sources for the acceleration of agrarian reform, which include the State and regional budgets; the involvement of the communities in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of agrarian reform. This Regulation describes also the impacts of the agrarian reform on the farmers and the indigenous communities, focusing particularly on the following aspects: legal ownership or use rights over the land; improvement of livelihood security and productivity; legal recognition and protection for the farmers’ land assets; reducing vulnerability to land disputes and expropriation; promotion of social stability and harmony in rural areas, through the strengthening of the farmers’ land rights and access; economic empowerment and status of farmers; improving the recognition of indigenous communities’ customary land rights; encouraging the indigenous communities’ participation in implementing and planning the reform.

This Decision establishes the rules and responsibilities for managing and monitoring processing factories in the Lao PDR by decentralizing authority across three levels: central, provincial, and district. The goal is to ensure efficient and uniform factory administration to support industrial growth and safety standards. Central Level focuses on macro-management, including drafting laws, managing large-scale or strategic factories, and issuing factory operation licenses for high-impact industrial sectors. Provincial Level is responsible for managing medium-scale factories within the province, issuing certain production certificates, and monitoring technical standards, safety, and environmental compliance. District Level manages small-scale factories, conducts field inspections, and monitors daily operations, hygiene, and the environmental impact of local industrial activities. The Decision also defines specific requirements for technical inspections, reporting structures, and the coordination needed among these different levels of government to manage raw materials, waste disposal, and factory safety.

Launched a new project to support small-scale and entrepreneurs to benefit from the country's national fruit. Nutritious jackfruit is one of the most important and widely grown fruits in the country, with a largely unexploited potential. The project, that will be implemented by FAO, is dedicated to promoting the production and marketing of jackfruit.

This Ministerial Regulation, in order to implement provisions of articles 16 paragraph (7) and 18 of the Government Regulation no. 26 of 2020 concerning Forest Rehabilitation and Reclamation, provides for preparing a General Plan for Forest and Land Rehabilitation in River Basin Areas and the Annual Plan for Forest and Land Rehabilitation. The Regulation concerns: river basin area, as a land area, which is an integral part of the river and its tributaries, to collect, store, and distribute water; watershed management; forest rehabilitation Plan; land rehabilitation Plan; critical land; water catchment area; water resources management; forestry ecosystem; spatial planning; protected area; cultivation area; reforestation; greening, as the activity of planting of trees outside the forest area, to improve the quality of the environment; agroforestry; urban forest, both on state and private land; mangrove ecosystem; terrestrial ecosystem; coastal management; erosion. The Regulation covers the following matters: procedures for preparing the Plans; governmental agencies involved; data collection including: social and economic data, biophysical data; development of water resources; erosion and sedimentation control; construction of water structures, including: retaining dams, water absorption wells, rainwater harvesting installations, drainage systems; assessment procedures for soil conservation and crops and trees evaluation; issuance of business permits for forest utilisation; classification of critical land categories in relation to disasters risk.

This Decision of the Lao Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry establishes the national standards for organic agriculture. Its primary objective is to manage and certify organic production to ensure ecological balance, enrich soil biodiversity, and reduce synthetic chemical use. The Decision sets up the rules, principles, and technical criteria for producing, processing, certifying, and labeling organic agricultural products in Laos. It defines organic farming, prohibited substances, conversion periods, soil and water management requirements, and restrictions on chemical fertilizers, pesticides, GMOs, hormones, and additives. It also describes standards for seeds, livestock, aquaculture, and beekeeping, ensuring practices that protect health, biodiversity, and the environment. The Decision further sets procedures for inspection, certification, and use of the “Laos Organic” label. It outlines responsibilities of producers, processors, traders, and government agencies regarding compliance, monitoring, and enforcement. Requirements for processing, storage, transportation, record-keeping, and import/export of organic products are detailed in the Text.

Implemented a duty-free treatment of 98% tariff lines goods originating from Bangladesh exported to China. Several kinds of basic leather products added into the 98% zero-tariff lines are good news to Bangladeshi exporters in the leather industry, which is a industrywith huge potential in Bangladesh. Businessmen in the leather industry have already been focusing on the opportunity provided by the 98% duty-free treatment.

This Regulation amends the Government Regulation no. 45 of 2005 on establishment, management, supervision and dissolution of State-owned enterprises, in order to optimise the role of these enterprises as development agents in supporting the national economy, through strengthening their institutions, organs and resources. Amendments concern: insertion of new paragraphs on appointment and revocation of board of directors’ members; insertion of new articles requiring the board of directors, and the supervisory board to comply with the constitutional provisions, while performing their duties; reasons for dismissal of a member of the board of directors; ministerial powers to dismiss Directors; measures on banning commissioners and members of supervisory board from becoming politicians; measures on appointment and revocation of commissioners and board of supervisors’ members; rights and obligations of State owned enterprises’ workers and compliance with the legislative and constitutional provisions; provisions on workers’ retirement.

This Technical Regulation establishes requirements for processing, manufacturing, transportation, storage, trade, export and import of meat and meat-based products. It shall also be applicable to import of pork, poultry products and fish products. It shall not be applicable to meta and meat-based products destined for individual private consumption. Livestock destined for slaughtering must be healthy and originate from areas and herds free of infectious animal diseases. Livestock destined for meat processing must be accompanied by veterinary certificate. It establishes hygiene and sanitary procedures for slaughtering of livestock and post-slaughtering treatment of carcasses. Meat and meat-based products packed in pieces or in bulk must meet food packaging and labelling requirements and standards. Raw and fully processed meat shall be transported separately.

This Regulation, consisting of 48 articles, provides governmental agencies, regional and local governments, experts, private sector and the community with guidelines for the prevention and control of zoonoses and of emerging infectious diseases, in order to overcome the threat of these diseases within the country and to prevent the social, economic and security outcomes of a potential disease escalation. The Regulation covers the following matters: information system for zoonoses and emerging infectious diseases; community-based and integrated surveillance on the incidence of disease or health problems and conditions that influence the increase and transmission of diseases; coordination of ministerial activity. The Regulation focuses on: risk assessment and mapping, scope and quality of surveillance, control measures and comprehensive responses; integrated system of surveillance between ministries, governmental agencies, local governments, private sector in the field of human and animal health; definition of emergency mechanism; monitoring, evaluation and reporting; funding for the implementation of prevention and control of zoonoses and other diseases. Appendices concern guidelines on: comprehensive joint risk assessment concerning the relationship between humans, animals and the environment; cross integrated surveillance of zoonoses and new infectious diseases through the One Health approach; definition of standards for disease surveillance; collection, transportation, storage and examination of specimens in the laboratory; definition of standards and procedures for surveillance technical development in the field of wildlife health; protection of wildlife health in conservation areas; mobilisation and sharing of resources in capacity building effort for disease prioritisation; implementation framework of a roadmap for strengthening the National zoonoses and emerging infectious diseases information system, including covid-19; research activity; training of surveillance personnel in health crisis management and disaster preparedness.

This Instruction establishes guidelines for the sustainable harvest and management of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) in Laos. Harvesting is permitted in specific zones, including production forests, forest land conversion areas, and village-use forests, provided they follow approved technical standards and sustainability practices. The document categorizes NTFPs into three lists to determine the level of oversight required. Products in List I require high-level approval from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, while List II items are managed by provincial authorities. List III products and registered cultivated medicinal plants do not require specific harvesting permits, allowing for seasonal collection by citizens as long as sustainability is maintained. The regulatory framework emphasizes inter-departmental coordination, particularly between the agricultural and health sectors, to monitor medicinal plants and verify their origins. Quotas for harvesting must be applied for annually and cannot be carried over from previous years. Regarding trade and logistics, companies must prioritize local processing before seeking export permits, which are restricted to non-prohibited species that cannot be processed domestically. Movement of NTFPs across different lists requires specific permits from either provincial or district offices, with additional health department clearance needed for medicinal varieties. The Department of Forestry and Forestry Inspection are tasked with monitoring compliance and ensuring all state obligations are met.

The scope of this Law is to regulate production, import, export, sale, consumption of alcoholic beverages, prevention of alcohol abuse, and combating alcoholism. It shall not be applicable to non-profit alcohol production with traditional raw materials for personal use; passage of liquors through customs for passenger’s personal use; and samples of liquors for international exhibitions. The number of special licenses for the production of alcoholic beverages shall be determined by the Government, taking into account the population density, location, and factory capacity. Special license for the production of alcoholic beverages other than those produced by traditional technology shall be distributed by the Government through auction sale. The special license for alcoholic beverages produced by traditional technology shall be granted, extended, suspended, restored, revoked by the governor of the province, capital, or the governor of the free zone based on the opinions and conclusions of the competent authority of the territory. The production of alcoholic beverages shall be carried out on the basis of a special license issued in accordance with the procedures specified in this law. The special license for the production of alcoholic beverages shall include information on the types of alcoholic beverages, production methods, raw materials to be used, location of the factory, and production capacity. Special license shall be non-transferable. The holder of a special license for the production of alcoholic beverages must meet the requirements for the supply of alcoholic beverages for sale and service that meet the requirements of standards, technical regulation, quality, and safety, and have obtained a certificate of conformity. The production of alcoholic beverages shall be carried out in accordance with technological procedures, sanitary and hygienic conditions, and approved standards with dedicated equipment with metered input and output of the line. Alcoholic beverages produced in Mongolia shall be labeled with the following information: (a) type and series number of alcoholic beverages; (b) name and address of the producer of alcoholic beverages; (c) package size; (d) number and designation of ingredients and food additives; (e) production date, month, day, storage conditions; (f) hardness of alcohol; (g) standards and technical regulations; and (h) information on the introduction of trademarks, good practices, and quality management systems may be placed on the label of alcoholic beverages. The requirements and warning model for the label of alcoholic beverages shall be jointly approved by the members of the Government in charge of food and health issues.

The Government, with a view of supporting national economy, production and export of value-added final products, shall perform the following arrangements to such purpose: (a) to support the manufacturing of final products by gradually increasing the level of processing of wool and cashmere, and to approve and implement production and trade technical regulation in connection with the production and export of cashmere with quality and standards that have been processed beyond hair separation from 2023; (b) draft a law on exemption from added value and customs duties for importation of industrial equipment intended for processing beyond hair separation; (c) annual formation of the necessary funding sources for the provision of low-interest, long-term, concessional loans in order to support the production of depilated wool, cashmere, cotton, spun yarn and finished products; (d) quality of yak wool ordered by processing plants to farmers and livestock owners shall be implemented by the relevant decision in the field of creation of the legal framework for the provision of monetary incentives to such purpose; and (e) a complex measure aimed at increasing the production of environmentally friendly and sustainable products by expanding the range of externally accredited laboratories for product certification complying with the international level, developing science, production and innovation, and improving the international competitiveness of wool and cashmere products.

This Presidential Regulation aims at increasing the availability, access, and the quality and safety of food consumption with strategic efforts to increase production and productivity, regulate distribution; at increasing agricultural productivity and strengthening human resources in agriculture and the application of technologies and innovation in agricultural sector. The Regulation concerns the following topics: agricultural management, including food crops, plantation, animal husbandry and agro-ecosystem conservation; farmers and their families; agricultural business actor; agricultural extension, as a learning process to help farmers and business actors to organise themselves in accessing market information in order to increase productivity, efficiency and raise awareness on the preservation of the environment; food; food availability; access to food; quality of food consumption. The Regulation provides for: implementation of agricultural extension in provinces and districts with a forum for the management of competency development of workers; strengthening of the working relationship; formulation of policies and drafting of plans on agriculture extension; monitoring and evaluation of activity; tasks and responsibilities of agricultural extension institutions in districts and villages; capacity building; agricultural extension materials, provided by the Minister taking into account: natural resource potential; availability of local food genetic resources; market development potential; availability of agricultural facilities and infrastructure; planting season and harvest schedule; food insecurity conditions and cases of malnutrition; local food availability. Specific authorisations is required for technological materials likely to damage the environment, disturb the health and cause economic losses. Specific agricultural extension materials to improve food availability, food access, and quality of food consumption include: cultivation and post-harvest food crops, horticulture, plantation, and animal husbandry, nutritious food preparation techniques, creation of community food reserves, integrated agricultural management, development of micro, small and medium enterprises in food distribution, food quality improvement.

The objective of this Law is to establish principles and regulations that foster a conducive environment for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) growth, including improved access to finance, technology, and markets. Businesses are categorized as Micro, Small, or Medium based on specific thresholds regarding the number of employees, annual revenue, or total assets. The state prioritizes MSME development through targeted policies, including tax incentives, credit facilities, and infrastructure support. Promotion Measures include: Utilization of the MSME Promotion Fund to provide low-interest loans and credit guarantees; Provision of training in entrepreneurship, management, and specialized technical skills; Facilitating participation in trade fairs, e-commerce adoption, and integration into regional and global value chains. The amended Law specifically emphasizes the adoption of modern technology and digital tools to increase productivity and operational efficiency. It encourages informal businesses to register formally by simplifying administrative procedures and offering one-stop-service registration models.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: This Decision, consisting of nine chapters and subdivided in 24 articles and implementing the Environmental Protection Law 2013 (Revised Version No. 29/NA), applies to individuals, enterprises, or organisations of both domestic and overseas that perform activities in Laos, and prescribes: measures on control, monitoring, and inspection of pollutions; measures to control pollution in case of emergency; the designation of hazardous areas; the identification of pollution risks linked to their impacts on the air, soil, water and public nuisance, in compliance with the National Environmental Standard threshold. The Decision is structured as follows: General provisions; Survey and registration of pollution sources and establishment of plans for pollution control and importation of waste and hazardous substances; Management and measures on air pollution control; Management and measures on soil pollution control; Management and measures on water pollution control; Management and measures on public nuisance pollution control; Preventive measures and pollution control in case of emergency and identification of hazardous zones and pollution risks; Adoption of international standards and technical intervention; Final provisions. Concerning registration of pollution sources, this Decision empowers the Office of the Natural Resources and Environment to conduct survey and registration of pollution sources of family and handcraft business, and the Department of Natural Resources and Environment to conduct survey and registration of pollution sources of industry, mining activities, infrastructure projects, agriculture and mega forestry. Concerning air, water and soil pollution control, the Decision provides for: preparation of air and wastewater treatment system; monitoring the air emissions and wastewater effluents on a regular basis; planting trees in accordance with environmental plans in order to prevent dust pollution; application of pesticides, fertilisers and other related substances; disposal, dumping, landfill and destruction of contaminated and hazardous substances.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: This Regulation, implementing provisions of the Law no. 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, and of the Law no. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Principles, and consisting of 40 articles, provides for control of abandoned areas and lands. The Regulation concerns: right to control, own, use and preserve the land; concessions and licenses; obligations of right holders and cultivation of lands. The Regulation focuses on the following abandoned areas: mining areas, plantation areas, industrial areas, tourism areas. Matters covered by this Regulation include: inventory of areas and lands indicated as abandoned; control, evaluation, designation and warning of abandoned areas and lands; utilisation of abandoned areas and lands for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes.

This Government Regulation, implementing provisions of article 12 of the Law no. 11 of 2020 concerning job creation, provides for implementation of risk-based business licensing, in order to improve investments and thus business activity. The Regulation covers the following matters: business licensing; risk, as potential losses, due to a combination of danger and hazard; special economic area; free trade area; standard certificate; statement of capability for environmental management and monitoring; micro, small and medium enterprises; monitoring activity; standard classification of Indonesian business activity; capital investment; integrated business licensing system. According to the Regulation, the implementation of risk-based business covers the following matters: norms, standards, procedures and licensing criteria; procedures for monitoring activity; funding. The implementation of risk-based business includes the following sectors: maritime affairs and fisheries, agriculture, environment and forestry, energy and mineral resources, nuclear energy, industry, trade, transport, health, medicine and food security, public works. For each sector the ministries and the responsible authorities provide guidelines, standards, parameters and risk analysis for issuing risk-based business licenses. Concerning the maritime and fisheries sector, business licensing consists of: marine space management, fish catching, fish transport, aquaculture, fish processing and fish marketing, salt production, biotechnology, utilisation of sea water for energy production, utilisation of protected fish species according to the provisions of the CITES Convention, limitation on the size of fishing vessels. Concerning the agricultural sector, business licensing consists of: plantation and seed production, crops, horticulture, food security, animal husbandry, animal health, agricultural facilities. Business licensing in the environmental and forestry sector is based on: forest utilisation, management of hazardous and toxic waste, waste water treatment, utilisation of environmental services in the protected areas, utilisation of wild plants and animal resources, utilisation of production forests, processing of forest products, utilisation of water services for energy production. The energy and mineral resources sector focuses on the following topics: oil and natural gas, electricity, minerals and coal, renewable energy, mining activity, nuclear energy. The Regulation also provides norms and standards for the water resources sector, including environmental conditions of water resources, method of collecting and disposing of water. Concerning health and food sector, the business licensing consists of: health services, medical devices, control of animal diseases, vectors and carriers, quality control of treated and processed food. Further matters covered by this Regulation include: procedures for supervision and monitoring risk-based business licenses; data and information collection; sanctions and penalties for government officials and for business actors in the different sectors.

This Regulation, implementing provisions of articles 86,87,88,89,90,91,94,104, and 185 letter b of the Law no. 11 of 2020 concerning job creation, provides for regulating the facilitation, protection and empowerment of cooperatives and micro, small and medium enterprises. The Regulation concerns: business licensing; special allocation fund formation of cooperatives; powers and duties of central and local governments in formation of cooperatives; cooperatives activity in trade and other sectors; compliance with sharia’s religious principles; financing measures; empowerment for cooperatives carrying out activities in the following sectors: trade, agriculture and farming, forest management and protection, maritime affairs and fisheries management, port water transport; increasing human resources capacities through education and training; standard and criteria for classifying micro, small and medium enterprises; integrated management of micro and small business activities; facilitation of intellectual property rights; subsidies and incentives for business activities.

This Governmental Regulation, implementing provisions of the Law no. 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, provides for spatial arrangement of the Indonesian territory, in order to implement the administration of spatial planning through definition of guidelines containing norms, standards, procedures and criteria; provide legal certainty and justice for all stakeholders in carrying out their duties, responsibilities, rights and obligations in the implementation of spatial planning. This Regulation concerns spatial planning, including space allocation for environmental protection and cultivation function; natural resources utilisation; urban area, whose main activities are non-agricultural functions; strategic area; public consultation; small and medium enterprises; land bank; forest area; marine spatial planning; zoning plan and the related activities; plan for zoning the coastal and island-coastal areas; coastal waters and maritime zones; protected area; ecosystem conservation and sustainable use of its resources; sea lanes and migration of marine species; local community; traditional fishery community, whose traditional rights are recognised in carrying out fishing and related activities; business permits. Matters covered by this Regulation concern: preparation of general and detailed spatial planning; data analysis; issuance of related permits for business activity in the sea and for granting of rights over land management; definition of land rights; spatial plans regarding air space, land space and marine space; long and medium-term development plan; compliance with International Maritime Law; achievement of equitable development and economic growth and stability; community participation in spatial management; disaster management and related data administration; integration of environmental studies in the formulation of National Spatial Plans; allotment of space on the beach border, rivers, lakes, ponds, reservoirs and springs water; water resources utilisation; utilisation of green open space in urban areas; involvement of local communities in preparation of spatial plans; provisions regarding procedures for implementation of integrated management in environmental analysis; valuation of hazardous and dangerous materials, substances and explosives for areas designated for military bases; protection of biodiversity, ecosystem, terrestrial and marine flora and fauna and endangered species; realisation of marine infrastructure network systems; fish resources management and conservation. This Regulation also provides for: valuation and definition of waters around natural world heritage sites in the sea and around environmental control areas. Space utilisation and utilisation activities concern: land tenure; building technical plan; utilisation of forest areas for development purposes; right of use of the resources of the territory; issuance of environmental impact certification and preventive assessment of the environmental impact of the activities.

This Regulation, consisting of 104 articles and implementing the provisions of Article 142 and Article 185 point b of Law no. 11 of 2020 on Job Creation, provides for: the right to manage, cultivate, build, use on land; apartment unit; land rights and management of underground and overground spaces; land registration. The following relevant terms are defined: land; State land or land controlled by the State, including: reclamation land, emerging land, land derived from relinquishment or submission of right, land derived from release of forest area, abandoned land, entitled land; right to manage; land rights; overground space; underground space; right renewal; land registration; abandoned land; destroyed land; land office. Matters covered by this Regulation include: right to manage, including: utilisation of land, determination of fees and tariffs, relinquishment of the right, abolition of the right, reclamation land; right to cultivate, build and use on land, including: time period and conditions of right to cultivate, people to whom the right is granted, the following obligations related to right to cultivate: exploitation of activities of agriculture, fishery and cattle breeding in accordance with the allocation and requirements, cultivation of land in a proper way, construction and maintenance of the environment infrastructure and facilities existing, improving the fertility of the land, preventing damages and maintaining the preservation of the environment, maintaining the conservation function of water body boundary, facilitating the development of public plantation, proper use of water and other natural resources on the land; abolition and relinquishment of right to cultivate; subject of right to build; time period and conditions of right to build; obligations and prohibitions related to the right to build; subject of right to use; time period and conditions of right to use; abolition of right to use; annulment of land right due to administrative defect; granting of right to manage and land right for small island and in water areas; destroyed land and revocation of rights; land registration; final provisions.

This Government Regulation, consisting of 302 articles, implements the provision of articles 36 and 185 letter b, of the Act no. 11 of 2020 regarding job creation, and aims at regulating: forestry planning; changes in designation and functions of forest areas; use of forest areas; forest management and preparation of management plan; social forestry management; forest protection. The following relevant terms are defined: forest, forest area, State forest, private forest, customary forest, conservation forest, protection of forest, convertible production forest, nature reserve forest area, forestry planning, inauguration of forest area, demarcation of forest area boundaries, forest management unit, watershed, use of forest area, integrated research, forest management, forest utilisation, timber and non-timber forest product utilisation, business permit and licensing, silvicultural system, reforestation fund, social forestry, community forest. Concerning forestry planning, the Regulation includes and specifies the following activities: forest inventory, inauguration and management of forest areas, establishment of forest management area, preparation of forestry plans. Concerning changes in forest areas and in their functions, the Regulation empowers the Minister to make the necessary changes taking into account the results of the integrated research. Concerning the use of forest areas, the Regulation provides for its application for the development of activities outside the forestry area and in compliance with environmental sustainability. Concerning forest management and preparation of management plan, it is implemented in order to obtain more sustainable community benefits. The Regulation implements social forestry management, in order to achieve forest sustainability, community welfare, environmental balance. Concerning forest protection, the activity is carried out on forest management area, on private forest area and on areas outside the forest area, in order to: prevent and limit forest damages caused by human actions, livestock, fire, natural events, pests; defend the interests of the State and the communities; improve environmental restoration. The Regulation also provides for supervision activities, application of administrative sanctions, and general provisions.

This Ministerial Regulation, consisting of 715 articles, in order to implement the provisions of article 60 of Presidential Regulation no. 92 of 2020 concerning the Ministry of Environment and Forestry, provides for increasing the efficiency and reorganising the functions, works and procedures of the Ministry of Environment and Forestry. The Regulation concerns: organisational positions, duties and functions, including: formulation and implementation of Policies in the field of forest area consolidation and sustainable environmental management, conservation of ecosystem and natural resources, increasing watershed river capacity, control of pollution and environmental damages, increasing the competitiveness of forest products’ industry, management of forest waste, hazardous and toxic waste, climate change control, forest fire prevention, forestry protection measures. Further matters covered by the Regulation include: administrative affairs; financial activities; foreign and international cooperation; environmental impact analysis and prevention; environmental audits and risks analysis; formulation of and implementation of Policies in the field of administration and management of natural parks, nature tourism parks, national reserves, hunting parks, wildlife reserves, utilisation of environmental services, conservation of species and genetic resources; biodiversity protection; measures to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Wild Flora (CITES); watershed and river basins management; land rehabilitation measures; control and supervision of the aquatic ecosystem; formulation and implementation of Policies concerning forest plant seeding and seeding activities, afforestation and reforestation programmes, soil and water conservation techniques. The Regulation further focuses on: measures for the rehabilitation of inland waters and mangroves; utilisation of timber and non-timber forest products; processing, marketing and distribution of forest products; water and air pollution control; damage to coastal and marine areas; formulation and implementation of Policies concerning water quality management and protection; land damage control; specific requirements and restrictions on wastewater disposal into the sea; measures for increasing waste reusing, waste reduction, recycling and circular economy; emergency response to deal with hazardous and toxic materials; implementation of measures and actions to reduce ozone depleting substances, and greenhouse gas emissions; climate change mitigation and adaptation measures.

This Ministerial Regulation, in order to implement the provisions of Article 52, Article 88, and Article 116 of Government Regulation Number 23 of 2021 concerning Forestry Implementation, focuses on: forestry planning, changes in the function and designation of forest areas, and the use of forest areas, measures for ensuring forest management, and legal basis for forest area management. The Regulation defines the following relevant terms: Forestry management; forest ecosystem; forest area; State forests; forest rights; territory of customary law communities; State forest area; customary forest area; conservation forest; protection forest measures, including: protection of ecosystem, water management regulation, preventing flooding and seawater intrusion, controlling erosion, and maintaining soil fertility; production forest; permanent forest; integrated forest management, including planning, research, development, education and training; forest inventory; forest boundary delimitation; forest area mapping; river basin area; change in forest area functions; use of forest areas for development purposes; integrated research; non-tax state revenue from the use of forest areas; compensation; adequacy of forest area; strategic environmental assessment; forest and land rehabilitation measures; forest management plan; utilisation of timber and non-timber forest products; forestry protection measures; forest conservation and reforestation programmes; forestry information system; forest monitoring; forest area map; forest area boundary map; geographic coordinates; natural and artificial boundaries; forest spatial planning; land rights; land control inventory; land acquisition; cultivated land; forestry extension; community empowerment; forest management unit; forestry development plan; forestry permit; food security; forest area specifically designated for the purposes of Food Security; administrative fines and sanctions; environmental planning; environmental management and environmental monitoring efforts; social forestry. This Regulation focuses on the following matters relevant to forestry planning and forest area management: conservation, protection and production; forest inventory, forest area confirmation, forest area utilisation planning, forest management unit formation, and forestry development planning; data collection, monitoring, and quality control requirements; protection of watershed; procedures for ensuring designation, boundary setting, mapping, and official determination of forest areas; formation of boundary commission teams at provincial and local levels, coordination, and documentation requirements; formation of forest management units to manage forest areas efficiently and sustainably; partial changes in forest area designation and functions, including approval procedures for releasing forest areas for non-forestry uses, utilisation approvals, and related spatial and legal assessments; procedures for settlements of land tenure and use inside forest areas, with roles for government, rights holders, customary communities; verifications and dispute resolutions through multi-stakeholder teams; monitoring, evaluation, and reporting requirements for forest planning, land use, and boundary management.

This Ministerial Regulation, implementing provisions of article 202 of the Government Regulations no. 23 of 2021 about Forestry Management, provides for: forest management, preparation of forest management plans, processing of forest products, forest utilisation, imposition of administrative sanctions concerning processing of forest products and forest utilisation. The Regulation concerns: biological natural resources; protected forest area; water management; flood prevention; controlling erosion; forest utilisation, including utilisation of timber and non-timber forest products; utilisation of environmental services; forest management unit; long and short term forest management plan; integrated business licensing system; standard certification; silviculture and forest cultivation system; marking of forest products to declare that products comply with sustainability standards; reforestation fund; forest waste. The Regulation covers the following matters: forest inventory, for obtaining data and information regarding soil type, species, population, and habitat of flora and fauna; definition of various protected areas; content of forest management plan; duties and functions of forest management unit; roles and responsibilities of local governments; activities for enhancing forest rehabilitation, including: identification of critical land, improvement of cultivation, strengthening community participation, plant maintenance, forest protection and security, forest fire control; identification and mapping of forest areas for food availability and security; criteria and indications for utilisation of protected forests; provisions for utilisation of wood and timber resulting from logging; procedures for application, extension or restriction of business permits for forest utilisation; business activities allowed in protected forests: cultivation of medicinal plants, beekeeping, livestock, fruit and vegetables cultivation, agroforestry, wildlife sanctuary and animal rehabilitation, wild animal captive breeding, natural tourism, water resources utilisation, protection of biodiversity. Further matters covered by this Regulation include: utilisation of timber for non-forest activities; processing of forest products; permit for processing forest products; assessment of sustainable forest management performance; legality of forest products; issuance of certificate; monitoring; forest product import declaration; administration of forest products; transportation and distribution of timber forest products; capacity building for private forest owners; penalties for forest exploitation.

This Ministerial Regulation, implementing provisions of Article 10 paragraph (4) of the Government Regulation no. 29 of 2021 concerning implementation of trade sector, provides for determining prohibited import of certain goods and prohibited export of certain goods. The Regulation defines free trade zone; prohibition from exporting goods of the following sectors: agriculture, including fertilisers; forestry, including wood types and species of trees; mining, waste, cultural heritage; prohibition from importing goods of the following sectors: food and nutrition, particularly sugar, rice; hazardous and toxic waste; non hazardous and toxic waste; medical devices containing mercury; hand tools in finished form; ozone depleting substances; used plastic bags, sacks and clothes; goods using refrigeration systems based on chlorofluorocarbon and hydrofluorocarbon. The Regulation defines conditions for re-import of prohibited goods, and for the return of exported goods, outside the customs area and the special economic zones, and provides for sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the legislation, in case of violation of its provisions. The attached schedules detail the various goods whose export or import is prohibited for each specific sector.

These Regulations provide for the compoundable offences under regulation 13 of the Singapore Food Agency (Certification Marks) Regulations 2019. The Chief Executive of the Singapore Food Agency, or an employee of the Agency authorised by the Agency for the purpose of section 44 of the Food Agency Act 2019, may compound any offence under regulation 13 of the Singapore Food Agency (Certification Marks) Regulations 2019.

This Ministerial Regulation, implementing provisions of article 51 paragraph (3) of the Law no. 7 of 2014 concerning Trade, provides for regulating the export of prohibited goods, in order to protect national security, public interest, cultural heritage, intellectual property rights, human and animal health, fish resources, plant and vegetation and the environment. According to the Regulation, the determination of prohibited goods is carried out on the basis of a ministerial or governmental proposal. The Regulation provides for sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the legislation, in case of violation of its provisions. Appendix I concerns goods of agricultural sector prohibited to be exported, including: natural rubber and derivates, tree and soil waste. Appendix II concerns prohibited goods in the forestry sector, including: rough wood, hoop wood, piles and pillars of wood, coniferous trees, wood from trees other than conifers. Appendix III concerns prohibited goods of the mining sector, including: natural sands of all kinds, other type of clay, various minerals and mineral substances, top soil.

The Bangladesh Veterinary Council established under the Bangladesh Veterinary Practitioners Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. XXX of 1982) shall be deemed to have been established as the Bangladesh Veterinary Council under this Act. The Council shall be a statutory body and shall have a permanent continuance and a general seal and, subject to the provisions of this Act, shall have the power to acquire, possess and transfer property, both movable and immovable, and may sue in its own name and may also be sued in that name. For the registration of a person as a veterinary practitioner, he shall apply to the Council in the prescribed manner and subject to payment of fees, including a certificate of educational qualification in veterinary subject with a degree recognized under schedule numbers 1 and 2 or sub-section (5) of section 15. (2) Upon receipt of an application under sub-section (1), the Council- (a) In the light of the criteria and policies prescribed by examining the information mentioned in the application and if any examination is taken under section 18, then if the examination is passed, then the person shall be registered as a veterinary practitioner; And (b) If the applicant is ineligible for registration, he shall not be registered and the application is rejected: inform the applicant of the reason for the same. The Council shall include in a registration book the names of veterinary practitioners registered under sub-section (2) and publish and preserve them. Registration shall be renewed by the registered veterinary practitioner every four (4) years in the manner prescribed. If a registered veterinary practitioner acquires any additional educational qualification or certificate in veterinary matter, the Council shall include such qualification against his name in the registration book in response to the application. Registration Out Of Evidence Act, 1872 (Act No. Shall be deemed to be an official document under I of 1872.

Since the Cruelty to Animals Act, 1920 exists for the purpose of raising social awareness to ensure animal welfare (I of 1920), in view of its provisions, it is appropriate and necessary to enact new laws reflecting the needs for the animal welfare. The Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for the rearing, transportation and slaughter of animals. The Act lays down a general principle establishing that animals should be treated well and with respect. An animal may not be subjected to unnecessary pain or suffering, and the animal's welfare may not be jeopardized unnecessarily.

The main purpose of this Act is to provides for the establishment of the Singapore Food Agency. The Act is divided into the following Parts: Preliminary (I); Establishment, Functions and Powers of Agency (II); Constitution and Membership of Agency (III); Decision-Making by Agency (IV); Personnel Matters (V); Financial Provisions (VI); General (VII); Transfer of Undertakings to Agency (VIII); Related and Consequential Amendments to Other Acts (IX); Saving and Transitional Provisions (X). The Act defines the Singapore Food Agency's internal organization and its powers and functions, which include: (a) to support regulation of the production of primary produce and animal feed to ensure the safety and wholesomeness of food supply in Singapore; (b) to support regulation of the handling and supply of food to ensure that it is safe and suitable for human consumption and to promote public health; (c) to support assessing and otherwise requiring that food produced in or imported into Singapore complies with Singapore food standards so as to ensure that it is safe and suitable for human consumption; (d) to support regulation of the construction, hygiene and operating procedures of premises, vehicles and equipment used for the handling or supply of food; (e) to support regulation of businesses engaged in the handling or supply of food so as to minimise food safety risks and to ensure the provision of information relating to food to enable consumers to make informed choices; (f) to promote fair trading in food; to develop food education initiatives, including the publication of information to increase public awareness of food supply resilience, food safety, food standards and food labels; (g) to protect and conserve fisheries and to regulate the fisheries industry, including the use and control of fishing ports and harbours; etc. The Act also amends the Fisheries Act, the Environmental Public Health Act, the Feeding Stuffs Act, the Wholesome Meat and Fish Act, the Health Promotion Board Act (Chapter 122B), etc.

The purpose of this Law is to diversify and develop small and medium-sized enterprises and services, improve their competitiveness, increase jobs, and increase their share in the economy. The purpose of this Law is to regulate relations establishing the scope, form, management, and legal basis for regulation of state support for small and medium-sized enterprises and services. This Law shall apply to domestic small and medium-sized enterprises and service enterprises registered in the state register with the aim of making a profit, permanently located and operating in the national territory. Small and medium-sized enterprises and service providers shall be intended business entities operating in the manufacturing, trade and service sectors with up to 200 employees and annual sales revenue of up to 2.5 billion tugriks. Cluster means a business entity that cooperates in a coordinated manner in terms of production and service objectives, types, directions, and geographical locations, in the form of cooperation or diversification. Small and medium-sized enterprises and service providers shall operate in the form of companies, cooperatives, or partnerships. A business entity that meets the conditions specified in this Law shall submit its application for registration as a small and medium-sized enterprise or service provider to the state administrative body responsible for small and medium-sized enterprises, or to the authorized person responsible for the relevant issue in the locality, in writing or electronically. The Government shall grant support to small and medium enterprises in the following ways: (a) financial support as credits and loans on preferential terms; (b) loan guarantees; (c) provision of equipment financial leasing services and lease interest support; (d) provision of tax relief and tax exempt; (e) support of the sale of products, works and services through public procurement; and (d) provision of business consulting services.

These Regulations provide for the rules to be satisfied for the application for, issuance of certificate or renewal of certificate. A certificate holder or a person who is authorised under these Regulations to use a certification mark must not transfer, assign or otherwise dispose of the certificate or authorisation. The Regulations further provide for the duration of certificate, the duty of certificate holder, penalties, etc.

The objective of this Act to ensure that investors are given any services, facilities, incentives, licenses, permits, clearances or permits required for any project or initiative proposed by them in order to implement domestic and foreign investment plans in the interest of rapid development of the lives of the people of Bangladesh. Unless there is anything contrary to the subject or context, Regional One Stop Service Centre means the Regional One Stop Service Centre referred to in sub-section (1) of section 5; (2) One Stop Service means the process of providing any service referred to in Schedule B by the Central One Stop Service Authority or Regional Centre under this Act;(3) Central One Stop Service Authority means the Central One Stop Service Authority referred to in sub-section (1) of section 4. Any of the following Schedules of the Act, namely:-(a) List of Central One Stop Service Authority Schedule-A; and (b) a list of services, facilities, incentives, licenses, permits, clearances or permit issuing agencies or authorities and services; (5) prescribed means defined by the rules; (6) focal point means services, facilities, incentives, licenses, permits, clearances or any person prescribed by the agency or authority issuing permits under sub-section (5) of section 4; and (7) service, facility, incentive, permit, clearance or permit issuance agency or authority means the agency or authority issuing services, facilities, incentives, licenses, permits, clearances or permits referred to in Schedule B.

This Ministerial Regulation amends the Regulation no. 59/M-DAG/PER/8/2016 concerning provisions for import and export of animals and animal products, in order to improve the activity of small and medium enterprises working in the sector of trade of animals and animal products, and to support the implementation of the import trade system through trans-boundary supervision. The Regulation defines: animals; ruminant; animal reproduction; animal products; animal diseases; labels and packaging; import and export activity; import and export authorisation; recycling mark for food packaging; State-owned enterprises. Amendments concern: release of export approval by the competent authorities; restrictions and limitations on animals and animal products export; duties and obligations of the enterprises, including proof of ownership of slaughterhouse and refrigerated storage rooms for animal products; release of import approval; request of specific certification for animal products imported from countries at risk of spreading diseases; inspection of compliance with import requirements. Attachments include lists of animals and animal products whose import is restricted, including: horses; goat and sheep; pigs; poultry; milk; butter; various types of cheese; meat and processed meat.

This Government Decision validates the List of acute infectious and contagious diseases and zoonotic diseases that pose a risk to human life, which entail a ban on the international trade of livestock, animals, raw materials and products derived from them (Annex 1), the List of highly contagious and infectious diseases that entail restrictions on the domestic trade of products of animal origin (Annex 2), and the List of other infectious (Annex 3).

This Order is issued to strengthen strictness of the management and inspection of endangered prohibited wild fauna and flora to bring them in line with the laws and regulations of the Government and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) as well as to effectively prevent negative impact on restricted wild fauna and flora. The Order requests: to stop the hunting of all wild animals listed in the prohibited list (Appendix I of the Order), stop the import, transit, export, trade of alive or lifeless wild fauna and flora; to stop the establishment of prohibited wildlife farm (Appendix 1) for business purpose and promote the existing farms to transform into safari or zoo environment for the purpose of conservation, tourism and scientific purposes only; to strictly prohibit the trade, import and export of prohibited wild flora with no authorization from relevant sectors.

The Bangladesh Rural Development Board Ordinance, 1982 is an act enacted for the purpose of revising it and re-enacting it in a timely manner. The functions of the Board shall be as follows: (a) assist primary cooperative societies, rural development teams and upazila central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies at the village level to become self-governing and economically sustainable driving forces under their own management for the purpose of increasing production; employment and rural development; (b) encourage primary cooperative societies and rural development groups to increase the income of the poor people of the village and to encourage employment; make maximum use of irrigation facilities depending on ground and surface water through the formation of rural development teams; (d) ensure productive use of institutional loans through cooperative societies, upazila central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies and rural development teams; and to help the members of that society or party increase the amount of shares and savings deposited; the objective is to encourage the adoption of multi-pronged activities, in particular, the marketing of agricultural products;( c) to provide fruitful training to rural development teams and members of the management committee of upazila central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies and ideal farmers in agricultural and rural development activities; services to rural development teams and upazila central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies, To maintain communication and coordination with the concerned ministries, divisions and agencies to provide supply and cooperation; (j) to encourage the district and national federations of upazila central cooperative societies or thana central cooperative societies to progressively conduct development, incentives and educational activities related to rural development;(z) to assign necessary financial and administrative powers to thana, upazila, district and division level employees to achieve the objectives and goals of the board; (j) prepare the annual development program of the board; (t) prepare or approve the annual budget as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of section 12; (l) present to the Government projects, programs and rural development models consistent with rural development and implement them with the approval of the Government; (d) to study or evaluate the progress of the implementation of the projects and programs taken by the Board and the problems arising from them, and whether the goals of such projects and programs have been achieved; etc. Without prejudice to the totality of the provisions of sub-section (1), the Board may perform its functions: (a) perform any function within the budget allocation approved by the Government or any special fund allocation, to bear any expenses, to procure the goods, services or equipment necessary for the use of the Board, and to execute the necessary agreements or agreements;(b) the Government for the purpose of preparing or receiving any plan or scheme, any agency, local government institution or agency or any agency or the government may, with the permission of the government, receive advice or assistance from any foreign government or agency; (c) coordinate the implementation of the policies formulated by the government for rural development and its related activities.

The government of Kazakhstan implemented a paperless document management system (e-Freight) for air cargo transportation through a public-private partnership. The project aims to digitize documentation processes to improve efficiency and transparency in air logistics. Following a trial period in 2018, the system was launched commercially in October 2019. It currently facilitates electronic data exchange between airports, airlines, and freight forwarders according to IATA standards. Future plans include integrating the system with the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Agriculture to further streamline trade processes.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project was initiated in December 2016 by a private consortium to modernize air cargo logistics in Kazakhstan. The initiative seeks to increase the attractiveness of the country as a transit hub and improve the overall efficiency of air cargo documentation. By moving away from paper-based systems, the project aims to reduce administrative burdens and enhance the speed of cargo processing.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of National Economy of Kazakhstan
beneficiaries: air cargo carriers, freight forwarders, airports

policydecision_details: This Regulation, implementing the provisions of Article 68 paragraph (3) of Sintang Regency Regional Regulation no. 1 of 2016 concerning Environmental Protection and Management, provides for land clearing activities and control and limitation of fire methods to be implemented by members of local farming communities in compliance with applicable laws and regulations and with traditional and customary rights. The Regulation provides the steps of land clearing: making land borders; logging and land clearing activity; waste utilisation to produce renewable energy; and requires each member of farming community to plant local varieties and comply with the prescribed methods of clearing, manually or mechanical. The Regulation concerns limited and controlled burning; air pollution emergency level; rights and obligations of members of farming communities; coordination of regional disaster management agencies; monitoring activity; financing.

Following the widespread distribution of the fungal disease myrtle rust, the New Zealand government decided in 2018 to cease active containment and eradication efforts. The current policy focuses on long-term management through scientific research and monitoring rather than active disease control. Landowners are not required to treat or remove infected plants, leaving management decisions to their discretion. The government continues to support research programs to understand the disease and mitigate its long-term impacts on native and ornamental plant species.
contextoradditionalinfo: Myrtle rust, caused by the fungus Austropuccinia psidii, was first identified in New Zealand in 2017. Initial response operations by the Ministry for Primary Industries and the Department of Conservation aimed to contain the spread, but the disease proved to be too widely dispersed by wind. Consequently, the response was closed in May 2018 to shift focus toward scientific investment and long-term impact reduction.

policydecision_details: The scope of this Law shall be regulation of mandatory enrichment of certain types of foodstuffs with a view of protection of public health and prevention of the deficiency of certain vitamins and minerals. The objective shall be to ensure safety of foodstuffs and conformity of standards and technical requirements set forth for foodstuffs. This Law shall be applicable to processing of foodstuffs containing certain vitamins and minerals, import and export thereof. Enriched foodstuffs shall be intended foodstuffs with food additives in the form of vitamins and minerals, in separate form or in mixed form. Food enrichment shall be intended addition of concentrated food additives containing vitamins and minerals in accordance with specific standard. Business entity performing manufacturing of enriched foodstuffs shall have the right to state support and incentives. Business entity performing manufacturing of enriched foodstuffs shall have the following duties: (a) to manufacture enriched foodstuffs in accordance with established standards; (b) to supply enriched foodstuffs to public certified by accredited laboratory; (c) to label enriched foodstuffs in accordance with the established modalities; (d) to register enriched foodstuffs with public authorities; and (e) to have equipment for the enrichment of foodstuffs. State inspector shall supervise food quality and standards of production of enriched foodstuffs and shall control trading organizations. This Law consists of IV Chapters divided into 13 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II regards arrangements for organizational activities. Chapter III regards supervision and control of enriched foodstuffs. Chapter IV contains miscellaneous provisions.

For the purposes of this Act, the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation established under the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation Ordinance, 1961 (E.P. Ord No. XXXVII of 1961) shall continue as if it had been established under this Act. (2) The Corporation shall be a statutory body and shall have a permanent continuance and a general seal and, subject to the provisions of this Act, shall have the power to acquire, possess and transfer property, both movable and immovable, and may sue in its own name and also be sued in that name. The Corporation shall perform the following functions, namely:- take necessary measures for the production, processing, warehousing and marketing of agricultural inputs relating to seed and horticulture development and supply to farmers directly or through dealers; take necessary measures to create and expand irrigation facilities in the agricultural sector; procure, transport, warehousing and supply fertilisers directly or through dealers to ensure the supply of fertilisers; build, repair and develop irrigation and irrigation and crop protection infrastructure; conduct surveys of irrigation machinery, irrigation areas, water resources, water quality, level and availability; research, experiments and creation of data banks; for the proper use of water for agriculture: surface and rainwater conservation and use; groundwater recharge, etc. The Corporation shall have the following powers in matters relating to land, namely:-(a) purchase, exchange, acquisition or otherwise acquire land; (b) all functions relating to land management, including land development; (c) land use functions described in the activities, programs and project documents; (d) conservation, sale, exchange or otherwise use of land; (e) lease at appropriate rent and under certain conditions.

In order to preserve endangered plant species, in particular Saposhnikovia divaricata (Turcz.) Schischk, recorded in the list of rare and protected plant species shall be prohibited collection and harvesting of the aforesaid species for the period from 1 January to 1 September for 5 years until 2023.

These Regulations are enacted in accordance with section 50(3) of the Sale of Food Act. Regulation 2 of the Sale of Food (Composition of Offences) Regulations (Rg 3) is amended by deleting the words “Food Establishments” in paragraph (c) and substituting the words “Non‑Retail Food Business”.

This Order stimulates classification, registration and digital encoding of waste.
