The objective shall be to use environmentally-friendly systems for the classification, collection, transport, storage, reuse, recycling, recovery, destruction and export of waste and to establish fees for waste service and information processing. Waste is categorized by source and type, and the code consists of 6 digits. Hazardous waste shall be classified in accordance with hazardousness risk.

The purpose of this information standard is to provide for mandatory country of origin labelling requirements for food for human consumption that is sold in Australia (including offered or displayed for sale). It does not impose labelling requirements on food sold outside Australia. Under this information standard, most food for retail sale in Australia must be labelled with a country of origin. There are different labelling requirements depending on whether the food was: grown, produced or made in Australia; packaged in Australia; grown, produced or made in another country; packaged in another country. In addition to a country of origin statement, the marks include an indication of the proportion of Australian ingredients by ingoing weight through text and a bar chart. If all of the food in a display or package was grown, produced or made in Australia, the mark will also include a kangaroo logo. In some circumstances, more detailed information can be voluntarily added to the text in a standard mark. If the food was not grown, produced, made or packaged in Australia, the labelling will be required to meet the requirements in sections 15, 16 or 17. Briefly, it must identify: the country of origin of the food, if it is from a single country (it may also identify where the food was packaged if this was a different country), or if the food is from more than one country the country where the food was packaged, if applicable and that the food is of multiple origins. For non-priority food the requirements for standard marks and the placement of origin statements in a box are voluntary, rather than mandatory. The non-priority foods are: seasonings; confectionary; biscuits and snack food; bottled water; soft drinks and sports drinks; tea and coffee; alcoholic beverages

This Presidential Regulation provides for defining the organisation and the duties and functions of the Food and Drug Supervisor Agency, in order to protect and improve the quality of life of the people, to increase national competitiveness, and to strengthen institutional supervision in the field of food security. The Regulation concerns the following matters under the Agency’s responsibility: drugs, medicinal substances, narcotics, psychotropics, addictive substances, traditional medicines, health supplements, cosmetics, and processed food; and the tasks of the Agency: preparation and implementation of national Policies, norms, standards and procedures in the field of drug and food control; implementation of supervision before and during transport and circulation of drug and food; implementation of technical guidance and supervision in the field of drug and food control; issuance of permits; conducting of investigations.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: This Ministerial Regulation, consisting of 24 articles and two Tables, aims to provide technical guidance for the restoration of the National Ecosystem for the following entities: Government; Local and Provincial Government; Communities, including indigenous and tribal peoples; and person in charge of business and/or activity. The Restoration of the National Ecosystem undertakes for damaged ecosystems in: ecosystems with protected forests or cultivation. The peat ecosystem with a protected function is damaged as referred to in paragraph (1), when it exceeds the preservation criteria as following: artificial drainage; exposure to pyrite and/or quartz sediments below the layer; and/or reduction in the area and/or volume of land cover.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: These Rules are framed by virtue of section 52 of the Wildlife (Conservation and Security) Act, 2012. The provisions of these rules are not applicable in some cases such as parks, zoos, private parks etc. The Rules require co-management committee to be formed for purpose of conducting activities for the management of protected area. They provide for the constitution and procedure for general committee and executive committee to be formed under the co-management committee. They provide for election of president and other administrative provisions in respect of the various committees. Duties and functions of co-management committee include formulation of action plan, management of biodiversity and natural resources, encouraging participation of local stakeholders, patrolling with the help of the community, supervision of afforestation and other such functions as mentioned therein. The Rules provide for the formation of village conservation forum to create awareness, encourage compliance, provide assistance to the committees and social forestry programmes. Formation of community patrol teams is also included in the rules. The Forest Department is required to define core zones, buffer areas, landscape and corridors in protected area and the adjoining area to facilitate forest management, mapping, survey and preparing maps. Sources of income in protected areas include nature tourism services, non-timber forest products including fisheries. The Rules also contains provisions relating to fund, its management and use.

These Regulations of the Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries prescribe standards and requirements regarding bananas placed on the market in South Africa. The Regulations prescribe quality classes and concern, among other things, quality standards, packing and marking of products. No persons shall place on the market bananas that are not conform to classes and standards as set out in these Regulations. The Regulations also concern inspection and sampling of consignments. The Annexes specify permissible cultivars and quality standards.

This Proclamation provides rules for the control of the quality shall apply to any person who directly or indirectly involves in coffee marketing and quality control of coffee. This Proclamation shall apply to any person who directly or indirectly involves in coffee marketing and quality control. Quality inspection shall be carried out by the legally designated regional quality control organ under the coordination of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority in accordance with this Proclamation. Coffee exporters shall register to National Bank of Ethiopia and notify to the Authority, the export coffee contracts of coffee purchased from the Ethiopia commodity Exchange or in other alternative transaction or produced in their own farm and coffee roasted, roasted and grinded sold in foreign market. The Proclamation defines other obligations of coffee exporters and of coffee roasters and handlers, and of domestic coffee traders and sellers. Any coffee transaction actor who buys or sells coffee outside the Ethiopia Commodity Exchange or other optional transaction centers established by Authority shall commit an offence.

In exercise of the power conferred under Chapters II and III of the Food Act of Bhutan 2005, the Ministry of Agriculture and Forests issues these Food Rules and Regulations of Bhutan 2017 to facilitate the implementation of the provisions of the Food Act of Bhutan 2005. These Rules, consisting of 109 sections divided into eight Chapters, apply to all stages of production, processing, transport, storage, distribution preparation, trade, import and export of food. It also applies to preparation, handling or storage of food for institutions and mass catering during public events. It does not apply to primary production for private domestic use or to the domestic preparation, handling or storage of food for private domestic consumption not intended for sale. These Rules and Regulations regulate all the activities related with food, such as: Labelling; Food Advertising; Labelling of Genetically modified food and ingredients; Responsible agency, Food inspector and Approved laboratories; Licensing of Food businesses and Food business operators; Requirement for Food safety licensing; Import/export of Food; Imposition of Penalties, etc. In addition, the Rules and Regulations define hygienic minimum requirements for food businesses and requirements and procedures for the licensing of food businesses, their operators and food handlers. Food shall be deemed to be correctly labelled if the relevant standards, guidelines and recommendations related to labelling of the Codex Alimentarius Commission or appropriate standards or requirements prescribed by the Ministry have been followed, and the information on the label does not mislead the purchaser or consumer. The licensee has the obligation to: ensure that food is handled, processed and stored in a way that the relevant food safety requirements as detailed in the Codex Recommended International Practice - General Principles of Food Hygiene, and where appropriate, the requirements of commodity-specific Codex Recommended Codes of Practice is complied with, so that contamination, growth and survival of pathogens or product deterioration is prevented.

This Ministerial Regulation defines procedures for imposition, collection and deposit of forest resources provisions, reforestation funds, compensation, fines for violation of forest exploitation and issuance of business licenses for forest utilisation. The Regulation concerns: non-tax State revenue; national forests; natural forests; right of use; customary forest; rehabilitated plantation forest; timber and non-timber forest products; business permits for utilisation of forest products; cultivation rights; drafting of plan and data collection. This Regulation focuses on forest resources provisions; various types of forest products; composition and utilisation of the restoration fund; procedure for imposing fines; control and monitoring; administrative sanctions and penalties for misconduct.

This Regulation, implementing provisions of article 36 E paragraph 2 of the Law no. 41 of 2014, concerns measures for importing livestock and animal products from Country or Zone within a Country of importation. The Regulation defines the following relevant terms: animals, as creatures whose entire or part of their life cycle is on land, water and/or air; livestock; animal products. The Regulation concerns the importation of animal and animal products under the following conditions: consequences of disasters; the need to stabilise national stock reserve or supply; lack of meat availability; importation of the following species: cows and buffalos; importation of livestock originating from a foot and mouth disease free zone, determined by the World Animal Health Agency; specific restrictions for importation from countries that are not yet free from foot and mouth disease, but provide a control programme based on the results of risk analysis, ensure adequate packaging and labelling requirements and animal products safety treatment.

This Import Policy Order 2015-2018, consisting of nine Chapters and completed by two Appendixes, have been developed in exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 (1) of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950 (Act No. XXXIX of 1950). It is a national policy order which shall apply to import all kinds of goods into Bangladesh. Test of radioactivity levels is mandatory for imported milk, dairy, edible oil, vegetable seeds and cereal products which may be used as food for human consumpation. A certification should also be submitted to the customs authorities. In case of import of milk and milk products, a certificate issued by the competent authority of the exporting country mentioning that these products are free form Added Melamine, the cows from which the milk originates have not been given Estrogenic Hormones and Hormone growth promotants (HGPs) treatment and the existence of the level of heavy metal are in accordance with Codex Standards, must be submitted to the customs authority by the importer. Additional terms and conditions to be applicable for the import of fish feed, poultry feed and animal feed goods include, inter alia, 1) the shipping documents must be accompanied by radioactivity-test reports from the competent authority of the exporting country and a certificate to the effect that the goods are fit for consumption by fish, poultry or livestock; 2) the imported fish feed must be free from harmful medicines, hormone and steroid including chloromphenicol and Nitrofuran; 3) In case of import of poultry feed and animal feed ingredients are to be inscribed on its packet and a certificate issued by competent authority of the exporting country to the effect that such feed goods are free from Chloromphenicol, Nitrofuran, Antibiotics, Melamine and Genetically Modified Organism is to be submitted. Tests for chloromphenicol, Nitrofuran and Melamine shall be conducted in the government approved laboratories just after arrival of these products at the port; 4) meat and bone meal, fish meal and protein concentrate can be imported with the prior permission from the competent authorities, and importers shall submit the following certificates: a ) the imported goods are free from harmful Antibiotics, including Chloromphenicol & Nitrofuran; b) the imported goods must be free from harmful chromium, by-product of tannery and melamine. Rice seeds shall be importable subject to the conditions prescribed in the Policy Order, including: (a) the importer shall submit a quarantine certificate furnished by the original supplier and a phytosanitary certificate, along with export documents from the Government agency of the seed exporting country; (b) in case of import of hybrid rice seeds, there shall be in the phytosanitary certificate that the seed is purified with hot water treatment and with approved pesticides; ( c) a quarantine certificate shall also be obtained from the Plant Protection Authority before clearing imported rice seeds, from the Customs Authority; and ( d) an import permit issued by the Plant Protection Authority for importing rice seed should be submitte. Importablity of pesticides shall be determined in accordance with the Pesticides Ordinance, 1971. Furthermore, Appendix-1 lists the controlled goods which are the goods banned for import, including a number of chemical insecticides and industrial chemicals under the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, such as DDT, polychlorinated biphenyl. In addition, country of origin must be mentioned on all products, product packaging or containers. However for importing coal, cotton, aluminum raw materials and export-oriented garment and industrial raw materials, country of origin is not required. According to the policy, ocean-going ships, oil tankers and fishing trawlers, cannot be imported if it is 25 year’s old.

This Regulation, consisting of 19 articles divided into four Chapters, regulates the Cooperation of Use of Forest Zones for Supporting Food Security. Purpose and objectives of this Regulation are: promoting cooperation in the use of forest areas to support food security as a reference for cooperating in the implementation of food crops and livestock development efforts to ensure the achievement of national food production, by applying the principles of good forestry governance. Development of food crops and livestock in forest areas, can be done by the following mechanism: a) changes in the allocation of forest areas through the release of forest areas or exchange of forest areas; b) the use of forest area in forest area through borrowing of forest area; and c) forest utilization. The development of food crops and livestock in forest areas can be done through co-operation mechanisms. Further provisions on the development of food crops and livestock in the forest area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in separate Ministerial Regulations.

This Ministerial Regulation, based on articles 74 and 75 paragraph (5) of the Government Regulation no. 6 of 2007, concerning preparation of forest management plans and forest utilisation, in its last amended version, provides for the approval for forest corridors construction and for corridor use agreement, in order to improve the increased use of forest areas and meet forest users’ needs, in term of transportation of forest, mining, plantation, agriculture and fishery products. The Regulation concerns: forest ecosystem; protection of biological natural resources; forest area; preservation of forest, animals and plant resources; water resources management; prevention of flood and sea water intrusion; controlling erosion; soil fertility maintenance; business permit for timber and non-timber use products. Matters covered by this Regulation include: requirements and procedures of application for approval for realisation and utilisation of forest corridors and specific provisions concerning protected areas, location of intensive crop cultivation and genetic resources areas; authorities responsible for issuance and submission of permits; provisions for utilisation of wood and forest products within the corridors; penalties and offences.

This Regulation lays down rules for the application of Regulations (EU) No. 1308/2013 and (EU) No. 1370/2013 as regards European Union aid for the supply and distribution of fruit and vegetables, processed fruit and vegetable products and fresh products of the banana sector, and of milk and milk products to children in educational establishments. It also lays down rules for accompanying educational measures and for certain related costs in the framework of the school scheme referred to under article 23 of Regulation (EU) No. 1308/2013.

This Regulation, consisting of 13 articles divided into seven Chapters, under the Government Regulation No. 6 of 2007 on Forest Management and Forest Management Planning, establishes Integrated Information System of Sustainable Forest Management (SFM) to keep the policy of self assessment be optimized, so that the trust given by the government to the license holder can be implemented properly. This Information System aims to further ensure the security of the State levies from forestry products. The scope of this regulation includes: a) Object and Time Enforcement of SFM Information Systems. b) Material Content of SFM Information System. c) Management and User Access of SFM Information System. SFM Management Information System is conducted by the Secretariat of the Directorate General of SFM, assisted by all Directorate of the Directorate General of SFM. The System can be accessed by the Permit Holders, Provincial Office, Directorate General of SFM and by Public proportionally.

This Regulation, consisting of 11 Chapters, regulates the Administration of Forest Products originating from Plantation Forest in Forest Production. It establishes that the Administration of forest wood from plantations forest in the forest production are intended to ensure the rights of the state over all the forest timber products originating from the plantations that used permission/management rights in accordance with the provisions of the legislation. The Administration of timber forest products originating from forest plantations in forest production aims to ensure the legality and orderly circulation of the forest products as well as making the data and information available. The scope of the forest product administration from forest plantation in the production forests covers the entire forest product from the forest plantation that is used by the forest manager/holder of a valid permit and implements the self assessment through SIPUHH.

This Regulation, consisting of 44 articles divided into 7 Chapters and four Annexes, establishes import/export of plant-originated feed materials into the territory of the State of the Republic of Indonesia. This Ministrial Regulation is aimed as the legal base in the provision of services in the Importation and Exportation of Plant-Originated Feed Materials into and from the territory of the Republic of Indonesia. The Objectives of this Ministrial Regulation are to: increase the country income; meet the domestic needs for and stabilize supply of Plant-Originated Feed Material Supply; and ensure that the Plant-Originated Feed Materials entered into the territory of the Republic of Indonesia are free from OPT, OPTK, agents of the infectious animal diseases, exotic animal diseases, as well as to meet the requirements of feed quality and safety.

This Regulation, consisting of 19 articles divided into seven Chapters and four Appendices, establishes the administrative procedures for forestry products originating from Private Forests. The administration of the private forest products is intended to control the circulation of forestry products aimed at protecting the rights, private rights and legal certainty in the ownership/control and transportation of forestry products from private forests. Forestry products use from private forest does not need logging permission. The certificate of origin of forestry products originating from private forests are either: a) Form of Transport; or b) SKAU (Letter of Origin). Every private forest products to be transported from the location of harvest or collection points around the logging area to the destination point, must have either Form of Transport or Letter of Origin (SKAU), which is a transport document for transporting private forests products that applies to the entire territory of the Republic of Indonesia. The use of Letter of Origin (SKAU) is used in the private forests outside Java, Bali and Lombok.

The Suicide Prevention Action Plan 2025-2027 is a strategic document developed by the Commissioner for Mental Health within the Spanish Ministry of Health. It aims to address suicide as a critical public health issue through a comprehensive, human rights-based, and recovery-oriented approach. The plan is structured into six main lines of action: quality information, awareness-raising, prevention in situations of vulnerability, prevention in all policies, a health approach, and a comprehensive approach. It emphasizes the need for multi-sectoral collaboration, involving not only the health sector but also educational, workplace, and community settings. The plan is designed to improve surveillance systems, reduce the underestimation of suicide rates, and implement both universal and selective preventive interventions tailored to specific contexts, in line with international recommendations from the WHO and EU Council conclusions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan is established in response to the recognition of mental health as a fundamental human right and a public health priority. It builds upon existing national strategies, including the Mental Health Strategy of the National Health System 2022-2026 and the Clinical Practice Guideline on the Prevention and Treatment of Suicidal Behaviour, to intensify efforts in suicide prevention.
